subject: Private deployment: key governance & jurisdiction — DPA review and subprocessor scope
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@finco.com>

Cc: Rahul Verma <rahul.verma@finco.com>, DPO FinCo <dpo@finco.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Private deployment: key governance & jurisdiction — DPA review and subprocessor scope

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood's Private offering (VPC/on-prem guidance) for a payments fraud model and have a handful of DPA questions we need to resolve before we can finalize a pilot: 

- Key custody: we need to confirm whether customer-managed keys are supported for model weights + inference logs, and what access your ops team retains if keys are customer-managed.
- Jurisdiction & data residency: if we deploy in our EU region on a hosted private VPC, can any Redwood staff (or subprocessors) access the data from outside the EU for debugging or patching?
- Subprocessors: please provide the current list and whether any subprocessor has cross-border maintenance access.

We're attaching our standard DPA checklist; can you point to the clauses you'd expect to sign vs. those requiring redlines? We also copied our legal partner Peter Su for redline coordination.

Goal: receive an explicit statement on access boundaries and a short proposed contract paragraph for customer-managed keys we can share with procurement by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Alice

--
Alice Jenkins

alice.jenkins@finco.com

Subject: Re: Private deployment: key governance & jurisdiction — DPA review and subprocessor scope

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I've attached our current DPA (DPA_Redwood_v3.1.pdf) and the up-to-date subprocessor roster. High level answers below; Vivek / Neha included for technical/legal precision and a short proposed clause.

- Customer-managed keys: supported. Customers can provide keys via KMS (Cloud KMS or customer HSM) and elect to have encryption at-rest + model artifact encryption tied to those keys. When customer-managed keys are active, Redwood does not hold the plaintext key material. Our ops team may request temporary, scoped access in emergencies, but that flow requires a formal request with justification, is logged, and must be approved by both the customer and Redwood security (see proposed emergency access clause attached).
- Access/jurisdiction: When deployed in customer's VPC/air-gapped on-prem installation, control plane signals are minimized. Redwood engineers do not have routine remote shell access to customer worker nodes. Maintenance or debugging that requires access is only performed under the emergency access process (customer approval + audit). For hosted private in specific cloud regions, telemetry about service health may traverse Redwood-managed control infrastructure; we can scope telemetry to EU-only regions and contractually prohibit cross-border debugging by Redwood staff.
- Subprocessors: the attached CSV lists vendors and their roles. A small number of subprocessors (e.g., GPU cloud provider for Dedicated, logging/observability vendor) have maintenance contracts that could be cross-border; we can mark those as "no remote access to customer plaintext" when customer uses customer-managed keys.

Next steps: Vivek, can you draft a short operational demarcation clause (technical bulleted responsibilities + emergency access flow) we can send to Peter/FinCo? Neha, can you provide proposed redline text for the DPA (key custody + access restrictions)? Alice — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Monica

--
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Private deployment: key governance & jurisdiction — DPA review and subprocessor scope

Thanks, Monica. Below is a concise operational demarcation we recommend including in the DPA (and/or an Appendix):

Operational demarcation (suggested language):
- Deployment model: For VPC/private deployments where the customer elects customer-managed keys (CMK), Redwood will not persist customer key material in its control plane. All model artifacts and inference logs stored on persistent volumes are encrypted with the customer's CMK.
- Access controls: Redwood staff require a documented, auditable change request for any access that would expose plaintext data or model artifacts. Requests must include: purpose, justification, duration, and affected resource identifiers. Customer approval (explicit sign-off via ticketing or email) is required prior to any access.
- Emergency access: In critical incidents where immediate access is necessary to prevent material harm to the service, Redwood may request temporary access. Such access is granted only after: (a) an emergency escalation call with customer-designated approvers, (b) time-limited access tokens provisioned via customer's KMS (no key export), and (c) post-incident full audit report delivered within 72 hours.
- Subprocessor isolation: Any subprocessor that requires maintenance access to compute hosting customer workloads must be under contract terms that prohibit exporting customer plaintext data and must be restricted to support tasks via pre-approved remote jump boxes. If customer uses CMK with non-exportable keys, subprocessors will not be able to decrypt persisted artifacts.

I'll attach a short doc with the above plus the expected ticket fields for approval flows. Also: operationally we can scope telemetry to EU-only endpoints and provide a signed attestation for region-limited telemetry flows.

-Vivek

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment: key governance & jurisdiction — DPA review and subprocessor scope

Monica / team — I reviewed the DPA and Vivek's operational demarcation. Below are two redlineable paragraphs to add to the Data Processing Agreement (suggested "Customer-controlled keys" and "Access & emergency procedures"). Please treat as starting language for negotiation.

1) Customer-controlled keys: "Where Customer elects to use customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs) for the encryption of model artifacts and inference logs, Redwood shall not have access to the plaintext key material or the ability to decrypt Customer Data unless Customer provides explicit, time-limited access in accordance with the Access & Emergency Procedures below. Customer retains sole control of the CMK lifecycle; Redwood is permitted to process encrypted artifacts for the purpose of providing the Service but shall not export or copy key material to any Redwood-managed key store."

2) Access & emergency procedures: "Regular support operations shall not include any action that exposes plaintext Customer Data. For any action that may expose plaintext Customer Data or require decryption, Redwood shall: (a) submit a documented support request including scope and justification; (b) obtain Customer approval by identified approvers; (c) access resources only via customer-designated jump hosts and time-limited credentials; and (d) produce a post-incident audit report within seventy-two (72) hours. In emergency situations where imminent harm is likely, Redwood may request emergency access which shall only be granted after a documented emergency call with Customer approvers and the issuance of time-limited credentials. Any emergency access will be logged and reviewed by both parties."

I can provide these as tracked changes in the DPA PDF or as a Word doc. I flagged a potential subprocessor concern for one vendor (observability vendor) that currently holds aggregated logs off-cluster; recommended change: aggregated logs must be pseudonymized and stored within EU region for EU deployments.

-Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

- For the observability vendor, we need the pseudonymization method and retention period. Can you confirm whether that vendor ever receives raw inference logs when customers are on CMKs?
- Peter will produce a redline this afternoon; Rahul and I will review and circle back.

Let's tentatively book a 30-min call for Thursday to walk procurement and security through the flow if you (Monica/Vivek/Neha) are available.
